tier1.text: The talus receives the body's weight from the tibia, or shin bone. The talus passes this weight backward to the calcaneus, or heel bone, and forward through the foot. Seven tarsal bones form the back half of the foot, and the talus is the highest. At the ankle joint, the talus meets the tibia and the fibula, a thin leg bone.

sentences.text: The talus receives the body's weight from the tibia, or shin bone.

quotes.quote: The talus bone of the foot receives the weight of the body from the tibia.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: tibia: shin bone; the large, weight-bearing bone located on the medial side of the leg
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The talus passes this weight backward to the calcaneus, or heel bone, and forward through the foot.

quotes.quote: The talus bone thus transmits body weight posteriorly to the calcaneus and anteriorly through the navicular, cuneiform, and cuboid bones, and metatarsals one through five.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: calcaneus: heel bone; posterior, inferior tarsal bone that forms the heel of the foot
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Seven tarsal bones form the back half of the foot, and the talus is the highest.

quotes.quote: The posterior half of the foot is formed by seven tarsal bones (). The most superior bone is the talus.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: tarsal bone: one of the seven bones that make up the posterior foot; includes the calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid, medial cuneiform, intermediate cuneiform, and lateral cuneiform bones
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: At the ankle joint, the talus meets the tibia and the fibula, a thin leg bone.

quotes.quote: talus: tarsal bone that articulates superiorly with the tibia and fibula at the ankle joint
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: fibula: thin, non-weight-bearing bone found on the lateral side of the leg
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
